newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-COWBOYS RE-SIGN FULLBACK JOHNSTON.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-COWBOYS RE-SIGN FULLBACK JOHNSTON.

text.p: The Dallas Cowboys announced Wednesday they have re-signed unrestricted free-agent fullback Daryl "Moose" Johnston to a five-year, $7.5 million contract.

The 31-year-old Johnston has played eight seasons in the NFL, all with the Cowboys. He rushed only 22 times for 48 yards and caught 43 passes for 278 yards and a touchdown -- bringing cheers of "Moose" from the fans each time he touched the ball -- but his main value is as Emmitt Smith's blocking back.

"Probably the happiest person in receiving this news about Daryl being our fullback again next year is Emmitt Smith," Dallas coach Barry Switzer said. "I know he has a big smile on his face now and is thrilled to death, along with our coaching staff.

"Daryl means so much to us in the fact that his position is a dinosaur," he added. "There are very few type of football players remaining today, in the systems that are employed offensively, a true, tough, hard-nosed fullback that actually is a guard that ends up most of the time in the backfield blocking for a tailback."
Johnston has never missed a regular-season or playoff game during his career, playing in 143 straight and starting 84 of the last 85. He was selected to the Pro Bowl in 1993 and 1994.

"There were problems off the field (last season), there were a lot of things, but I've been here since 1989 and I know what this organisation is about," Johnston said. "I know what the players on this football team are about."
He said he believed the team could get back to the form that brought three Super Bowl championships in four years from 1993 to 1996 before stumbling last season.

"Since they (team management) pointed out maintaining the core and nucleus of this football team, and keeping that together, these are the guys that are going to bring Dallas back to the place that it was in the recent past," Johnston said.
The re-signing was better news for the Cowboys than the recent losses because of salary cap limitations of kicker Chris Boniol, to Philadlephia, and punter John Jett, to Detroit.
